title: Lockdown surface policy Terraform module for private deployments
creator: Lena Chen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that enforces a least-privilege network surface for Redwood private (VPC) deployments. The module will provide opinionated defaults and composable primitives for: (1) security groups with explicit allow-lists and default deny rules; (2) subnet-scoped NACL layers for coarse egress/ingress filtering; (3) split-horizon private DNS configuration (resolver, conditional forwarding, private hosted zones); (4) centralized egress policy bundles (HTTP proxy endpoints, allowed CIDR lists, outbound SNI controls); and (5) runtime health checks and upgrade hooks used during automated module rollouts. The goal is a single module package that platform teams can import to secure new private clusters and for the upgrade pipeline to apply safe, reversible changes with observable health gates.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes clear variables and outputs: sg_templates, nacl_layers, private_dns_config, egress_policy, healthcheck_config
Default SG/NACL state is deny-all with configurable allow-lists per tier (control-plane, infra, customer-tenant)
Private DNS supports conditional forwarding to customer resolver + Redwood resolver, with documented split-horizon tests
Egress policy supports: proxy endpoint declaration, CIDR allow-list, domain SNI allow-list, and per-environment overrides
Health checks implemented as Terraform provisioner + optional lambda probe for endpoints; module emits a healthcheck topic for Console alerts
Module includes a blue/green-safe upgrade path: canary apply policy and automatic rollback trigger when health gates fail
Automated unit/integration tests run in CI using tftest/localstack; acceptance tests for plan/apply and drift detection
Documentation (README + design doc link) and security review checklist completed and signed off
End-to-end staging deployment validated and performance/regression metrics captured
comments: 2026-01-10 Lena Chen: Scoped initial requirements with Platform and Security. Decided to combine SG + NACL + DNS + egress into a single opinionated module with extension points. Linked initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+Surface+Policy

2026-01-18 Daniel Park: Prototype SG templates and NACL layering in a spike branch. Found that some existing customer clusters rely on wide egress CIDRs; added egress_policy.overrides to support gradual tightening.

2026-01-21 Security (Amir Hassan): Reviewed and requested: (a) KMS-encrypted storage for proxy credentials, (b) audit events exported to Datadog and S3, (c) nullable enable_flag for IPv6 egress. Added to security checklist.
2026-01-29 PM (Rhea Gupta): Requested that private DNS support both Route53 and CoreDNS-based on-prem resolvers. Agreed to provide an adapter interface variable private_dns.provider.
2026-02-04 Eng (Daniel Park): Implemented healthcheck_config that publishes to an SNS topic. Added canary_apply.sh helper for staged terraform applies and rollback on failed health probes.
2026-02-10 Eng (Daniel Park): Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345 — includes module core, examples, and unit tests. Requesting review from infra and security.
2026-02-15 Design feedback (Aisha Patel): Documentation needs a clear migration path for existing clusters; added migration guide and a terraform import checklist.

2026-02-20 QA (Miguel Ruiz): Ran integration tests in staging. Found intermittent DNS flapping during canary NACL updates. Follow-up: introduce 30s stabilization window and probe retries before finalizing rollout.
